_note: Glossary (spec 7B.11). 'match' lists the words that are underlined and open the entry. Add an entry here and it works everywhere.

terms.definition: Sending a radio signal. A device cannot usefully receive on a shared antenna while it transmits.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: Listening for a signal. Receiving is very sensitive, so a nearby transmit can drown it out.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: Bluetooth Classic divides time into 625 microsecond slots. Packets start on slot boundaries and last one, three or five slots.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: A Bluetooth radio changes channel again and again, and each change is a hop. Classic hops every slot across 79 channels.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: The range of frequencies a transmission covers. A Wi-Fi 20 MHz channel has a footprint about 20 MHz wide; a Bluetooth hop covers 1 MHz.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: How many decibels weaker a transmitter's signal is at the other radio's receiver, thanks to antenna spacing and filtering. More is better.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: Desensitisation: a strong nearby signal makes a receiver deaf to weak ones. It is the main harm when isolation is low.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: The rule that decides who gets the air when Bluetooth and Wi-Fi both want it. How it decides is an implementation choice.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: Bluetooth stops hopping onto channels that are busy, such as those under a Wi-Fi channel. It needs time to notice and to agree the new map with the peer.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: Extended synchronous connection: a Bluetooth Classic voice link with reserved slots and a limited number of retransmissions.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: Advanced Audio Distribution Profile: streaming stereo music over Bluetooth Classic. It buffers audio, so it tolerates small delays but not long ones.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: The low-power Bluetooth. It works in short events at fixed intervals and uses 40 channels of 2 MHz.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: A scheduled exchange between two BLE devices. If one is missed, the next chance is a whole interval later.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: A connection event the link depends on. Missing too many in a row breaks the link, so anchors are protected.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: How long a Bluetooth link may go without a good packet before it is declared lost.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: A number that says how much a block deserves the air. It is not fixed: it rises as the need becomes urgent.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: A buffered stream is critical when so many packets are waiting that it is close to running dry. Its priority is raised.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: Sending a packet again after it was lost or corrupted.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: A moment when a Bluetooth block and a Wi-Fi block overlap and also interact: shared antenna or core, overlapping frequency, or low isolation.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: An overlap that does no harm, for example when the radios are well isolated.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: Both blocks went out but were probably corrupted, because their frequencies overlapped.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: A margin added on each side of a Wi-Fi channel to allow for leakage into neighbouring frequencies.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: One antenna serving both radios, usually through a switch. Only one can use it at a time.
terms.label: STANDARD

terms.definition: A processing core that runs a radio's firmware. Radios on one core cannot act at the same instant.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: An arbitration policy that gives the air to Bluetooth for a fixed share of each slice and to Wi-Fi for the rest.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: The stretch of time the tool simulates, for example 100 milliseconds. Results are only about that stretch.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: A number that fixes the random choices, such as which channel a hop lands on. The same seed always gives the same result.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: Two radios on one core taking turns in time rather than running at the same moment.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: The antenna switch and filters between the radios and the antenna.
terms.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

terms.definition: Wi-Fi waits a random short time before sending, so that devices do not all start together.
terms.label: STANDARD
